newsitem.title: GERMANY: European drugs industry presses EU on price issue.
newsitem.headline: European drugs industry presses EU on price issue.

text.p: European pharmaceutical companies on Monday appealed to the EU for help in tackling trade problems resulting from the import of cheap drugs from nations where prices are controlled by governments.
Industry representatives presented their case to EU Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann and health ministry officials from several nations.

Bangemann said discussions at the so-called Frankfurt Roundtable, hosted by the European Federation of Pharmaceutical Industries' Associations (EFPIA), laid the groundwork for more discussions and suggested another set of meetings.

"Both the fixing of prices by governments and the attempt to separate markets by companies in reaction to that fixing of prices are out of step with a world where so many barriers have been removed," Bangemann said after the day-long discussions.

Drug companies, reacting to a decision by the European Court of Justice allowing the cheap import of drugs from Spain and Portugal, were particularly concerned about finding a way to fight the effects of "parallel trade."
Parallel trade refers to importers buying drugs outside of official distribution channels in low-price countries and selling them in high-price ones.
Companies suggested the Commission grant the industry an exemption from EU competition rules to allow them to restrict the cross-border trade of their products under some circumstances.
Bangemann said the talks were useful but said a decision would not be possible immediately. "Clearly we are not going to reach an agreed position today," he said.

He said he was not wholly opposed to some forms of price control, as these are needed in the case of new innovative drugs where there may be a monopoly situation and a lack of market mechanisms to regulate prices.

But he rejected suggestions that abolishing price-controls would create a two-tier medical system with only the very rich being able to afford medical care. "At the moment there is no risk of a two tier system," Bangemann said, urging some deregulation to foster price transparency.

Bangemann also acknowledged the need to raise European companies' competitiveness in innovative new technologies by laying the proper groundwork. "We need to re-create an entrepreneurial culture in Europe. This is a task for all of us."
The roundtable was convened to agree on the main obstacles to the achievement of a single market and outline priorities in pricing and reimbursement policies for medicines.
